mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% for two consecutive months indicates labor market deterioration that precedes corporate earnings declines, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE remains above 5.0% for 3 months but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous CPIAUCSL YoY growth above 2.5% and FEDFUNDS at or below 0.25% creates stagflationary pressure that reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition holds for 3 months but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, industrial production below 100.0 signals manufacturing contraction that precedes earnings deterioration, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: During late-cycle expansion, INDPRO < 100.0 but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales above 600,000 million dollars reflects strong consumer spending that supports corporate revenues, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS remains above 600,000 million dollars for 3 months but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 1,600,000 units indicates cooling real estate activity that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: HOUST remains below 1600.0 for 3 months but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in payroll employment below 146,000 thousand and industrial production below 100.0 signals broad economic weakness that depresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition holds for 3 months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, federal funds rates above 2.0% increase equity discount rates, compressing valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.
